programme.title: Science and Technology
programme.degree: Bachelor of Science (BSc), 3 years, 180 ECTS, 50 student places
programme.how_found: WebSearch (allowed_domains ut.ee) 'University of Tartu bachelor Science and Technology English-taught programme admission' -> first result https://ut.ee/en/curriculum/science-and-technology; page header quote: 'Level of study Bachelor's Study language English Duration and credits 3 years 180 ECTS Form of study Regular study Location Tartu Student places 50 Tuition fee €6,000 per year'
programme.notes: No English-taught computer science bachelor exists at the University of Tartu. The only computer science bachelor is the Estonian-taught Informaatika. cs.ut.ee/en/admission (Institute of Computer Science): 'You can study Computer Science at the Bachelor's level at the Institute of Computer Science. The programme is in Estonian.' ut.ee/et/oppekavad/informaatika: 'Õppeaste bakalaureuseõpe Õppekeel eesti keel ... Toimumiskoht Tartu Õppekohtade arv 225 Õppetasu tasuta' and 'Kandideerimiseks peab sul olema keskharidus või sellele vastav haridustase (nt kutsekeskharidus) ja eesti keele oskus vähemalt B2-tasemel.' Science and Technology (specialisations: genetics and biotechnology, bioengineering and robotics, chemistry and materials science) is the English-taught bachelor's in the Faculty of Science and Technology and is recorded here as requested; it is not a computer science degree. ut.ee bachelors-and-masters page: 'In 2026 we offer admission to 28 English-taught programmes: 3 first level programmes and 25 master's level programmes'.

english.quote: IELTS Academic the minimum required score is 6.0 and no part can be below 5.5
english.how_found: Programme page -> 'English language proficiency – please see our acceptable tests and exempt categories' link -> https://ut.ee/en/english-language-requirements (also surfaced by WebSearch 'University of Tartu bachelor's admission international students English language requirements IELTS TOEFL')
english.notes: Same minimums apply to all English-taught bachelor's and master's programmes. TOEFL iBT: 'For the exams taken before 21 January 2026, the minimum required score is 75 (on the 0-120 scale) For exams taken on or after January 21, 2026: Minimum total score: 4 (on the 1-6 scale) Minimum section scores: Speaking: 4, Reading: 3.5, Listening: 3.5, Writing: 3.5'. Cambridge English (B2 First/C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency): 'the minimum required result is 169'. PTE Academic: 'the minimum required score is 59'. Only TOEFL iBT, IELTS Academic, Cambridge English and PTE Academic 'taken no more than 2 years before applying' are accepted; General Training IELTS and TOEFL ITP are not. Exemptions cover only secondary or higher education completed in English in an EU/EEA state, Switzerland, UK, USA, Canada, Australia or New Zealand, so a Kazakhstan NIS English-medium diploma does not exempt. Test results must reach UT by the bachelor's deadline (15 April). For the Estonian-taught Informaatika bachelor the requirement is instead Estonian at B2 level ('eesti keele oskus vähemalt B2-tasemel'). st.ut.ee/faqs still shows an older IELTS 5.5 figure; the ut.ee requirements page (6.0/5.5) is treated as current.

value.description: No minimum secondary-school grade average is published. Admission is by a 100-point composite score: higher/senior secondary school result in Mathematics (20%), result in Biology, Chemistry or Physics (20%), motivation letter (20%), online entry test (20%), admission interview (20%). An application enters the admissions ranking only with a total of at least 66 points; the motivation letter, entry test and interview each require at least 51 points to pass.

gpa.quote: The application will be considered for the admissions ranking if a total score of 66 points or higher is achieved. The maximum total score is 100 points.
gpa.how_found: Programme page https://ut.ee/en/curriculum/science-and-technology -> section 'Admission requirements' / evaluation of applications
gpa.notes: Supporting quotes from the same page: 'higher/senior secondary school result in Mathematics (yields 20% of the final score)'; 'The maximum score for the motivation letter is 100 points and minimum positive score 51 points.'; entry test 'To pass the test you must get at least 51 points.' No minimum grade in Mathematics or in Biology/Chemistry/Physics is stated and the page does not publish how school grades are converted to points. The Kazakhstan entry on the country-specific requirements page lists the accepted certificates (e.g. 'Аттестат об общем среднем образовании ... / Жалпы орта бiлiм туралы аттестат' with its supplement) and states no minimum grade. For the Estonian-taught Informaatika bachelor the published thresholds are 'Kandideerimiseks peab punktisumma olema vähemalt 66.' and 'Vastuvõtu tagab 80-punktise lävendi ületamine.'

deadline.notes: This is the 2026 cycle (autumn 2026 intake); the autumn 2027 deadline is not yet published. Programme page: 'Admission deadlines, admission requirements, and descriptions of the entrance examinations for the 2027 intake will be added to the website by the end of December.' Programme-page timeline (no year shown): '2 January Application system opens 15 April Application deadline 1 June Admission results 31 August Academic year starts'. 2026 entry test 8-9 May 2026 (online), interviews 14-22 May 2026. Applicants graduating in Kazakhstan may apply with current grades ('in Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgystan, Moldova, Russia,Tajikistan, Ukraine, Uzbekistan') by submitting the most recent transcript by 15 April; final documents by end of July. Non-refundable application fee EUR 100. Informaatika (Estonian-taught) 2026 window: '15. juuni Algab avalduste vastuvõtt 30. juuni Lõpeb avalduste vastuvõtt'.

tuition.notes: Confirmed on the main programme page https://ut.ee/en/curriculum/science-and-technology: 'Tuition fee €6,000 per year' (page states 'Curriculum version: 2026/2027'). 2027/28 fees are not yet published. ut.ee/en/content/cost-tuition: 'Starting from the academic year 2026/2027, the university will no longer offer tuition waivers to newly admitted students from countries outside of EU/EEA.' and bachelors-and-masters page: 'NB! There are no tuition waivers on English-taught bachelor's programmes.' Non-EU admitted students: 'Admitted students from other countries are required to pre-pay half of the first semester's tuition fee'. The official 2026/27 fee table PDF on adr.ut.ee (linked from cost-tuition) could not be opened (HTTP 503 / connection reset). The Estonian-taught Informaatika bachelor is free: 'Õppetasu tasuta'; cost-tuition page: 'All Estonian-taught degree programmes are free of charge for full-time students.'

value.name: Tuition fee reduction
value.detail: University of Tartu tuition fee reduction scheme (25%, 50% or 100% for one semester at a time); for Science and Technology BSc, eight admitted students receive a 50% reduction for their second semester, granted automatically on the weighted average grade of the first semester

scholarship_exists.quote: Tuition fee reduction In selected programmes, the university offers tuition fee reductions of 25%, 50%, or 100% for one semester at a time. For this programme, eight admitted students will receive a 50% tuition fee reduction for their second semester
scholarship_exists.how_found: Programme page https://ut.ee/en/curriculum/science-and-technology -> section 'Tuition fee reduction' (scheme described on https://ut.ee/en/content/cost-tuition, table row 'LT Science and Technology (BSc) 8 50%')
scholarship_exists.notes: This is the only university-run fee concession an incoming Science and Technology applicant can be considered for; it is not awarded at admission but after the first semester. cost-tuition page: 'Students do not apply for tuition fee reduction, it is granted automatically.' No tuition-waiver places exist on English-taught bachelor's programmes and from 2026/27 no waivers for non-EU/EEA newcomers (see tuition notes). ut.ee/en/content/scholarship-information: 'All English-taught bachelor's programmes are fee based.' and FAQ: 'Limited number of scholarships are available for international degree-seeking students.' CONFLICT: st.ut.ee/apply-now (under '2026 Intake') still says 'On the basis of the admission results, a limited number of applicants of both EU/EEA/Swiss and non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizenship will receive a stipend to cover their tuition fee.' and st.ut.ee/faqs says '5 best applicants will be given tuition-waiver scholarships' — these contradict the current ut.ee statements and appear outdated; verify with the admissions office. For the Estonian-taught Informaatika bachelor there is the 'Specialisation stipend of information technology curricula' (IT Academy stipend, https://ut.ee/en/content/specialisation-stipends-information-technology-curricula): '240 euros per month' for Computer Science bachelor's students, available 'from the first semester of his/her matriculation year', for students who are citizens of Estonia or reside in Estonia on a residence permit.

scholarship_international.quote: All students admitted in 2026 will be eligible to be considered for a tuition fee reduction based on their academic performance and the following criteria: they study full-time; are not on academic leave; have not exceeded the nominal duration of the curriculum;
scholarship_international.notes: The tuition fee reduction is open to all admitted students with no citizenship condition; the ut.ee cost-tuition page introduces it precisely as the replacement for tuition waivers that non-EU/EEA newcomers lose from 2026/27 ('However, some study programmes will introduce tuition fee reductions.'). Granted automatically for the second semester based on first-semester weighted average grade; eight recipients at 50%. The st.ut.ee stipend paragraph (if still valid) also states eligibility for 'both EU/EEA/Swiss and non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizenship'.

access_notes: The official 2026/27 tuition fee table (PDF on adr.ut.ee, the university's document register, linked from https://ut.ee/en/content/cost-tuition) returned HTTP 503 twice and a connection reset via curl; the fee was taken from the programme's own pages instead.

https://ut.ee/en/curriculum?... (curriculum search filtered to English-taught bachelor's) renders its result list with JavaScript; the fetched HTML contained no programme list. The count of English-taught first-level programmes (3) was taken from the bachelors-and-masters page instead.

There are no tuition waivers on English-taught bachelor's programmes.', IELTS 6.0/5.5). ut.ee central pages were treated as authoritative.
